records.mapping_rationale: Art. 32(1) requires the controller and the processor to implement technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk, including the ability to ensure ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems (point (b)). Art. 32(4) requires steps to ensure that people acting under their authority who have access to personal data process it only on instructions. Controlling who can reach personal data is one such measure.
requirements_covered: Limiting access to systems that hold personal data to named, authorised people (supports Art. 32(1)(b), confidentiality)
Removing access promptly when people leave, and reviewing access (supports Art. 32(4))
exclusions: Choosing the level of security appropriate to the risk (the opening words of Art. 32(1)): the kit gives no risk assessment for the user's processing
Pseudonymisation and encryption (Art. 32(1)(a)) are addressed by other controls
Instructing staff and contractors to process personal data only on instructions (Art. 32(4)) is not templated
dependencies: KIT-PRV-01 (knowing what personal data is held)
records.limitations: Art. 32 is risk-based: whether a measure is appropriate depends on the processing, so this mapping shows relevance, not sufficiency.

records.mapping_rationale: Art. 9(4)(c) requires financial entities to implement policies that limit physical or logical access to information and ICT assets to what is required for legitimate and approved functions, with policies, procedures and controls on access rights and their sound administration. requirements_covered: Least-privilege logical access, role-based access, enforced MFA and an access review (supports Art. 9(4)(c) and the authentication part of Art. 9(4)(d))
exclusions: Physical access is not covered
The documented policy set, and the 'relevant standards and dedicated control systems' for strong authentication, are not specified
Protection of cryptographic keys is addressed in KIT-SEC-01
records.limitations: This duty is owed by a financial entity. A startup supplier is not directly bound by it; a financial-entity customer may require equivalent measures by contract (contractual flow-down). Art. 9(1) to 9(4)(f) were read; the text after the change-management sentence of Art. 9(4) was not.

records.mapping_rationale: Art. 32(1)(a) names pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data among the measures to consider, as appropriate. Encryption is only as strong as the handling of keys and credentials, which this control addresses.
requirements_covered: Keeping keys and credentials out of code and in a secrets manager, with an owner and rotation (supports effective encryption)
exclusions: Deciding which personal data to encrypt or pseudonymise, and how, is not decided by this control (see the encryption and key management policy template)
Pseudonymisation is not covered
records.limitations: Art. 32(1)(a) is a measure to consider as appropriate, not an absolute duty to encrypt everything. Art. 32 is risk-based: whether a measure is appropriate depends on the processing, so this mapping shows relevance, not sufficiency.

records.limitations: Art. 25 depends on the state of the art, cost and risk. This mapping shows relevance, not sufficiency.

records.mapping_rationale: Art. 25(2) requires measures ensuring that, by default, only the personal data necessary for each specific purpose is processed, including as to accessibility. Keeping real personal data out of development and demo environments limits how much of it is processed and who can reach it. Separating environments also supports the confidentiality and integrity of processing systems (Art. 32(1)(b)).
requirements_covered: No production personal data outside production
Separate credentials and access per environment
exclusions: Product defaults (what is collected and who can see it by default) are not covered
Art. 25(2) also concerns the extent of processing and the period of storage by default; those are covered in the privacy process, not by environment separation
records.limitations: Art. 25 depends on the state of the art, cost and risk. This mapping shows relevance, not sufficiency.

records.mapping_rationale: Art. 32(1)(c) asks for the ability to restore the availability of, and access to, personal data in a timely manner after a physical or technical incident. Art. 32(1)(d) asks for a process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of security measures. A scheduled restore test is both a check of the recovery capability and such a test.
requirements_covered: Backups, snapshots and versioning that allow personal data to be restored
A scheduled restore test with measured timings, which tests the effectiveness of the backup measure
exclusions: 'Timely' is judged against the organisation's own needs: the kit measures recovery time but does not set the requirement
Recovery from incidents other than data loss (for example loss of a whole region or account) is only partly covered
Testing the effectiveness of security measures other than backups is covered in other controls
dependencies: KIT-GOV-01 (recovery objectives set by the business)
records.limitations: Art. 32 is risk-based: whether a measure is appropriate depends on the processing, so this mapping shows relevance, not sufficiency.

records.mapping_rationale: Art. 12(1) requires documented backup policies and procedures specifying data scope and minimum frequency, and restoration and recovery procedures and methods. Art. 12(2) requires backup systems that can be activated without jeopardising security and requires periodic testing of backup and restoration procedures. Art. 12(3) requires restoration using systems physically and logically segregated from the source and securely protected.
requirements_covered: Automated backups, restoration into a scratch environment, comparison and timing, and periodic restore tests (Art. 12(2) periodic testing)
Restoring into an environment separate from the source (supports Art. 12(3))
exclusions: Documented backup policies specifying data scope and minimum frequency by criticality or confidentiality (Art. 12(1)(a)) are not templated
Redundant ICT capacities (Art. 12(4)) are not covered
Requirements specific to central counterparties, central securities depositories and data reporting service providers are not covered
records.limitations: This duty is owed by a financial entity. A startup supplier is not directly bound by it; a financial-entity customer may require equivalent measures by contract (contractual flow-down). Art. 12(1) to (5) were read in part (to the start of paragraph 5).

records.mapping_rationale: Art. 24(1) requires the controller to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, taking into account nature, scope, context, purposes and the risks, to ensure and be able to demonstrate compliance, and to review and update them. Art. 24(2) adds data protection policies where proportionate. Art. 5(2) is accountability.
requirements_covered: Written roles, a scored risk register, short policies and an annual management review (supports reviewing and updating measures)
Policy templates for classification, retention and continuity (supports Art. 24(2))
exclusions: A GDPR-specific data protection policy set is only partly provided (see privacy/)
Using approved codes of conduct or certification to demonstrate compliance (Art. 24(3)) is not covered
The kit does not assess the risks to individuals that Art. 24(1) refers to
records.limitations: Community draft. Accountability means keeping real evidence; this mapping shows what the kit offers.
